Class GyroDifferentialPilot

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.GyroDifferentialPilot
All Implemented Interfaces:
Pilot
public final class GyroDifferentialPilot extends Object implements Pilot
A Pilot over two EncoderMotors whose power the program sets directly, such as a Powered Up hub's, that closes both loops itself with a DirectionFinder, a GyroHeading for instance. Every control period:
  • Travel: a DifferentialDriveOdometry keeps the pose from the encoders and the direction, along the line the robot faced at the start. A HeadingHoldController steers to a heading that leans back toward the line, so a drift is taken out, not just stopped from growing, and the travel ends when the progress along the line reaches the distance. The power ramps up from the minimum to the cruise power and back down near the end, so the wheels do not coast past.
  • Rotate: the robot spins in place toward the direction it had plus the turn, slowing down near it; it brakes inside the tolerance, settles, and nudges again, either way, while the settled direction is still outside it.

With an ObstacleDetector, a forward travel reads it every obstacle check and brakes when the way is blocked, ending with MoveOutcome.OBSTACLE; a rotation and a backward travel do not read it, since the detector looks ahead. A range read can take a while (an ultrasonic ranger waits up to 30 ms for no echo), which is why it is read less often than the motors are commanded.

Motors are seen from the robot: forward power drives the wheel forward and the count grows, whichever way a motor is mounted, so wrap a mirrored motor to turn both around. A stop() from another thread is seen at the next period. Waiting uses Thread.sleep(long, int), so a GyroHeading's thread keeps its turns. Create it once at startup; its moves allocate nothing.

    • GyroDifferentialPilot

      public GyroDifferentialPilot(EncoderMotor left, EncoderMotor right, DriveGeometry geometry, DirectionFinder direction, Clock clock)
      Creates the pilot. geometry converts the encoders to millimetres; its track width is used only for a heading from the wheels when the direction finder gives none, which a GyroHeading never does.

    • setTurnSlowdownDegrees

      public void setTurnSlowdownDegrees(int degrees)
      How far before the target a rotation starts slowing from its maximum power toward its minimum, in degrees. A robot that overshoots the target and swings back and forth needs it to start slowing earlier.

    • setTurnBrakeLeadMillis

      public void setTurnBrakeLeadMillis(int millis)
      How long the robot keeps turning after the pilot sends a stop, in milliseconds: the radio's delay and the robot's momentum. A rotation then brakes that far ahead of the target, at the rate it turns, instead of overshooting it and nudging back and forth. Zero, the default, brakes at the target.

    • setSteering

      public void setSteering(int correctionAtQuarterTurn, int maximumCorrection)
      How hard a travel steers to its heading: correctionAtQuarterTurn is the power correction a 90 degree error would get, so 270 is 3 power per degree, and maximumCorrection bounds it. A gain too high for how late the heading arrives makes the robot weave about its line; halve it if it does. Set it before the first travel.

    • setLineCorrection

      public void setLineCorrection(int millidegreesPerMillimetre, int maxMillidegrees)
      How far a travel leans its heading back toward its line: millidegreesPerMillimetre per millimetre off it, at most maxMillidegrees. A steep lean turns a small offset into a large heading change, another cause of weaving.

    • travel

      public boolean travel(int millimetres)
      Description copied from interface: Pilot
      Drives straight by millimetres, forward when positive, and waits until it ends. Returns true when the travel completed, false when it failed, timed out or was stopped; Pilot.travelledMillimetres() then says how far it got.
